transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Israel could soon have a new prime minister.
Gadi Isincott is making progress in his bid to unseat Benjamin Netanyahu.
It's still unclear when Israelis will next go to the polls.
In PRs, Daniel Estrin reports the hardest part of Isincott's push to take power may
still be ahead.
The opposition is made up of a core block of four parties, and this is a very eclectic
bunch.
There's a hard right party, there are two center-right parties, there's a left-wing
party, they're all Jewish parties.
So that's the core opposition, but they alone are not enough to build a stable governing
majority.
They just simply don't have the numbers.
So they need additional parties to join their coalition.
And this is where it gets tricky because this block of parties simply don't agree with
each other ideologically.
They might succeed in luring one of Netanyahu's traditional allies into the government, an
ultra-Orthodox Jewish party.
That's NPR's Daniel Estrin reporting from Tel Aviv.
Today is Black Friday, and retailers are counting on it to be the busiest shopping day of the
year.
NPR's Alina Saliuk reports that holiday spending is expected to set a record this season.
The National Retail Federation estimates that almost 183 million people will be shopping
this long Thanksgiving weekend.
This number is actually a bit lower from last year, but the overall holiday spending is
expected to keep rising from last year.
Part of it is that things are costing more because of inflation, but goods are actually
not climbing in price as fast as gas prices or housing costs or even groceries to some
extent.
So in surveys, shoppers are saying they expect to maybe cut back on travel or outings but
spend on family and the holiday.
Alina Saliuk, NPR News.
U.S. lawmakers are investigating how children can be exposed to online predators on the
gaming platform Roblox.
At a Senate hearing this month, two survivors told lawmakers they were groomed and sexually
abused by men they met on the site.
NPR's Ritu Chatterjee reports.
One of the witnesses at the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing was Woody Doe, a Marine
Corps veteran.
Doe, who used a partial pseudonym at the hearing, told lawmakers that as a child he loved Roblox.
Like millions of children, I discovered Roblox and quickly became hooked.
But he alleged that the platform exposed him to a predator.
Eleven.
That's how old I was when I was groomed and sexually assaulted by a man I met on Roblox.
He's among dozens of survivors who've sued Roblox for its role in exposing them to predators.
Roblox told NPR that safety has been central to the company and it now requires users to
verify their age to communicate with others and only allows kids of similar ages to communicate
with each other.
Ritu Chatterjee, NPR News.
This is NPR.
Nearly a million homes and businesses lost power Thursday as storms disrupted Thanksgiving
travel.
High winds and coastal flooding hit parts of the East Coast from North Carolina to New
York, New Jersey declared a state of emergency, and Macy's moved its Thanksgiving Day parade
to Saturday over safety concerns.
Farther inland, a winter storm brought heavy snow to Missouri and Illinois.
Record tides flooded parts of the California coast.
Hundreds of flights were delayed or canceled across the country.
According to FlightAware.com this morning, there are a little more than 400 delays within
into or out of the U.S.
The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria says supplies of a generic HIV
prevention drug have arrived in Zambia.
Michael Koloki reports the medication is expected to be delivered to other African countries
in the coming months.
The drug, known as linocupivir, is developed by U.S. pharmaceutical company Gilead Sciences.
Gilead has licensed a number of generic drug makers to manufacture and supply generic versions
of the drug to several low- and middle-income countries.
The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria said that deliveries of generic
linocupivir supplies are expected in Uganda in the coming days.
Several other African countries are set to obtain the drug in coming months.
Linocupivir, a long-acting drug administered twice a year, offers an alternative to daily
pre-exposure prophylaxis pills.
Last year, the WHO recommended the drug as an additional HIV prevention option.
For NPR News, I'm Michael Koloki in Nairobi, this is NPR News.

topics.text: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot makes progress in bid to unseat Netanyahu
Black Friday expected to set holiday spending record, with 183 million shoppers forecast
Senate hearing investigates predators exploiting children on gaming platform Roblox
Storms cut power to nearly a million homes and businesses, disrupting Thanksgiving travel
Global Fund reports generic HIV prevention drug lenacapavir arriving in Zambia
